question: the mandatory panel names one-hot ridge and the arms ledger contains it ZERO times -- what happens to the existing claims when it is actually run?

PREREGISTERED.margin_derivation: INHERITED verbatim from the arm acceptance bars so this stays commensurable with every arm it is compared against. Not re-chosen.

ADDS_NOTHING_OVER_GC.consequence: the existing baseline ladder stands; no arm's claim changes, and the panel's one-hot requirement is satisfied by a number that happens to add nothing. This is the outcome that CLEARS the back-run.

RE_READS_CLAIMS_BELOW_IT.when: one-hot median > gc median + 0.02 AND it exceeds at least one arm that reported a GAIN
RE_READS_CLAIMS_BELOW_IT.consequence: every arm it exceeds had its gain measured against a floor lower than the panel requires; those claims must be restated against this baseline before they mean what they say. The arms are NOT invalidated -- their reported MARGIN is.

DOMINATES_FROZEN_EMBEDDING.consequence: a 600-feature linear model matches the frozen 128-dim atlas embedding, which would make the embedding arm's contribution the open question rather than its headline. The largest possible finding here.

PREREGISTERED.gate: GC seed0 0.3000 and median 0.3112, both within 0.01, or REFUSE with exit 2

onehot_swept_SECONDARY.why_saturation_matters: if every seed picks the grid MAXIMUM the tuning wanted more regularization than offered, so the sweep does NOT bound the model and cannot support 'this is not a regularization artifact'. The grid was extended once for exactly this.
onehot_swept_SECONDARY.note: tuned on a TRAIN-INTERNAL 75/25 split, test never consulted. NOT the comparable number -- every arm was run at alpha=1.0.

excluded_off_substrate.fragment-rung-321k-rows-size-lever-LB-M9: off-substrate ('fragment' in name/evidence): a 150 bp TILE Spearman is not comparable to a FRAGMENT-ceiling fraction; the ledger's own SCOPE NOTE forbids it
excluded_off_substrate.pyramid-4scale-2.22decades-499bp-fragmen: off-substrate ('fragment' in name/evidence): a 150 bp TILE Spearman is not comparable to a FRAGMENT-ceiling fraction; the ledger's own SCOPE NOTE forbids it

consequence: the existing baseline ladder stands; no arm's claim changes, and the panel's one-hot requirement is satisfied by a number that happens to add nothing. This is the outcome that CLEARS the back-run.
honest_limits: Bounds a LINEAR ONE-HOT model on this substrate under this protocol. Not a claim about any arm's architecture.
Exceeding an arm does NOT invalidate that arm -- it invalidates the MARGIN that arm reported, because the margin was measured against a floor lower than the panel requires.

alpha=1.0 is the arm's own default and is deliberately NOT tuned for the primary. A 600-feature model and a 1-feature model do not share an optimal penalty, so the swept number is reported separately and is not comparable to the arms.
One substrate (44,106 peak tiles), one geometry (native 150 bp), one metric (Spearman).
